 Sabres at Flyers | How to watch, lineup notes, and storylines 
 Alex Lyon is expected to make a third straight start in net.
 By 
 Jane McNally 
 Sabres.com 
 November 17, 2026 
 Link copied 
 The Buffalo Sabres will look to get back into the win column as they take on the Philadelphia Flyers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Tuesday at 7 p.m.
 Buffalo’s latest blemish – a 2-0 loss to the Dallas Stars on Saturday – stretched the winless streak to four games. The 8-8-4 Sabres are now 1-4-1 in their last six, scoring just nine goals over that stretch. 
 It was goalie Jake Oettinger who did the heavy lifting in keeping Buffalo off the board on Saturday, but the Sabres are still searching for consistent offense as they tighten up their defensive game, too. Buffalo took a step in the right direction by holding Dallas to just one even-strength goal, but an 0-for-5 night on the power play took the spotlight. 
 “A lot of looks tonight, especially me in the third,” said forward Jack Quinn after the game. “Couldn’t solve [Oettinger], so definitely frustrating when you don’t score." 
 The Sabres' lineup could look a bit different on Tuesday as the team searches for a spark offensively.
 “Just trying to look at getting some guys going,” coach Lindy Ruff said after Monday’s practice. “Looking at trying to get (Josh) Doan some more opportunities, some better chances 5-on-5. … We’ve got to get (Ryan) McLeod scoring. We’ve got to get (Josh) Norris scoring. We’ve got to get more guys on the board to be effective.” 
 Monday's practice report | Ruff breaks down lineup changes 
 Up next: the second of Buffalo’s three meetings with the Flyers. They are 2-3-2 in their last seven, the latest a 5-2 loss at home to the Edmonton Oilers. Philadelphia handed Buffalo a 3-1 loss at KeyBank Center back on Oct. 21. 
 Here’s everything you need to know ahead of puck drop.
 How to watch 
 TV (Sabres broadcast market): MSG (Pregame coverage begins at 6:30 p.m.) 
 Streaming (Sabres broadcast market): DAZN 
 Streaming (out of market): ESPN+
 Radio: WGR 550 / Buffalo Sabres App 
 **More ways to watch/listen to Sabres games** 
 Lineup notes (updated 11:40 a.m.) 
 Of note from Monday's practice lines:
 Zach Benson and Tage Thompson were kept together on the top line. Together at 5-on-5 this season, Benson and Thompson have controlled 60.84 percent of expected goals and been on the ice for 10 goals for and just two against, per Natural Stat Trick.
 Jiri Kulich joins the top line at center, where Ruff feels he's "played his best hockey."
 The third D-pair had Olen Zellweger taking shifts with both Zach Metsa and Louis Crevier. Crevier played a season-low 6:10 on Saturday in Dallas and took just one shift in the third period as Buffalo pushed for offense.
 Alex Lyon had the starter's net at the optional morning skate, indicating a third straight game for the veteran after recovering from his preseason upper-body injury. The Sabres have lost the last two in spite of Lyon's efforts: .909 save percentage and 1.39 goals saved above expected (Stathletes).
 Here were the practice lines from Monday. Check back during 6:30 p.m. warmups for any potential changes.
 Notable numbers 
 Saturday’s loss in Dallas was just the second regulation road loss for the Sabres this season. Buffalo has earned points in eight of its 10 away games (4-2-4). 
 Thompson played a season-high 22:40 on Saturday, attempting five shots and putting four of those on net. His 79 shots on goal this season are tied for ninth-most leaguewide. 
 Quinn has five points (1+4) in his last five games. He attempted a team-high nine shots Saturday.
 Among Sabres players with at least 100 faceoffs taken, Norris leads the way with a 50.7-percent win rate. He won nine of 12 in Dallas on Saturday.
 Scouting the Flyers 
 Philadelphia is in the thick of a stretch of eight games in 14 days. Just two of those are home games – Sunday’s loss to the Edmonton Oilers, and Tuesday’s game against Buffalo. 
 The Flyers faced some injury troubles earlier on in the season but are nearly back to full health. Forward Denver Barkey, who scored twice Saturday before missing Sunday's game due to illness, participated in line rushes during the Flyers' morning skate. 
 Cole Knuble is also expected to play after three recent games as a healthy scratch. He scored the first two goals of his NHL career in Buffalo back in October.
 And Joseph Woll is expected to start in net. The first-year Flyer is 3-6-2 with a .902 save percentage in 11 starts, including wins in his last two.
